fleet.hoursPerBusIntro: Every bus of the fleet, the most used first; buses not used are at the end with 0 h. Click a bar to see that bus in detail.
fleet.hoursPerBusLabel: Hours in service per bus, the most used first
fleet.how1: The fleet is every bus ever seen on the live feed. A bus is in use when it reported a line in the window.
fleet.how2: Hours in service come from the recorded positions (every 10 seconds): each report on a line counts until the bus's next report, up to a minute, so gaps in the feed don't count as service. Days are service days, 03:00 to 03:00.
fleet.how3: Broken down, as on Abnormal trips: a trip run in full by two buses of the brigade, one taking over midway, where the replaced bus wasn't used again that day. It is back at its next report on a line after that day.
fleet.how4: Runs are consecutive reports on one line, brigade and headsign, at most 5 minutes apart; a gap of 30 minutes or more between runs is a break.
fleet.how5: Abnormal trips of a bus: trips it broke down on, and trips of its brigade it missed (not run while it ran the brigade's other trips that day). A cancelled trip (no bus on the brigade all day) has no bus to show it on. Only the city timetable's (BKM) lines can be judged.
fleet.searchPlaceholder: Number or model, e.g. 230 or Urbino
fleet.runsIntro: Each run in this window on its own row: consecutive reports on one line, brigade and headsign.
fleet.daysIntro: One row per service day (03:00 to 03:00): its runs on lines, and breaks of 30 minutes or more.
fleet.redDot: A red dot marks a day with an abnormal trip of this bus (listed below).
fleet.noLine: This bus served no line in this window.
fleet.noTrouble: It broke down on no trip and missed none of its brigade's trips in this window.

desc.cancelled: Not run: no bus ran the brigade at all that day.
desc.missed: Not run, while the brigade's bus ran other trips that day.
desc.lost: The bus stopped reporting midway and didn't come back to its brigade.
desc.short-turned: Run only partly: the bus, reporting all along, joined midway, or left more than 3 stops before the end (within the last 3, only turning onto its next trip 3+ min less late).
desc.detour: Run in full, but off its route (over 150 m away) for a while.
desc.vehicle-changed: Run in full, but by two buses: one ran part of it and another bus of the brigade took over midway (a breakdown, typically).
desc.no-signal: The bus stopped reporting partway (or started late) but was back for its next trip: most likely run, unseen.

anomalies.oldNewHeading: Old bus heading to {{old}}; new bus to {{new}}
anomalies.detourNote: Detour: {{m}} m off the route for {{min}} min, {{from}} → {{to}}
anomalies.detourMap: Line {{line}}: detour {{from}} → {{to}}, {{m}} m off the route
anomalies.how1: Every trip of the timetable scheduled to run in the window (for any part of it) is matched to the recorded positions: a report belongs to the trip of its brigade and line scheduled to leave its next stop closest to the report's time minus its delay (the headsign helps, but the feed's don't always read as the timetable's).
anomalies.how2: Seen is the stretch of the trip the bus reported heading to. A trip counts as run in full when first seen heading to one of its first 3 stops and last to one of its last 2 (reports come every 10 seconds).
anomalies.how3: Only a bus reporting all along (reports at most 90 s apart) shows that it short-turned; when its reports stop and it comes back for its brigade's next trip, it's a gap in tracking (no signal). A detour is 3 reports in a row more than 150 m from the trip's route shape, between its first and last stops. A bus change needs both buses to report at least 3 times on the trip under its brigade, one after the other, the first past the trip's first 3 stops and the second going further than the first got. A change on a trip run only partly is described in its note. The replaced bus is possibly broken down when it isn't used again that day: it doesn't move 500 m away and keep reporting a brigade for 10 minutes (a broken bus keeps reporting where it stands, sometimes under its brigade's other trips); otherwise it was reassigned to another line or brigade, or came back to the same brigade later.
anomalies.how4: A trip is judged as soon as it's clear what the bus did; until then it's under way. Trips during a gap in recording (3 minutes or more without any report) aren't judged. A trip not seen 10 minutes after it was due is listed as missing "so far" until 15 minutes after its scheduled arrival; a bus is lost after 15 minutes without reports. Only lines in the city timetable count.

hotspots.summary: Buses{{onLine}} stood still away from stops {{count}} times, for {{lost}} ({{perDay}} a day over {{days}} recorded). {{hotspots}} hotspots hold {{share}}% of that time.
hotspots.loseMost: Where buses lose the most time
hotspots.intro: Each hotspot with the time buses stood still there altogether, the most first. Click a row to show it on the map.
hotspots.none: No place where buses repeatedly stood still in this window.
hotspots.how1: Standstill: a bus on a line reporting twice or more in a row (every 10 seconds) within 10 m. Its time counts from the first of those reports to the last, so waits shorter than about 10 seconds are mostly missed.
hotspots.how2: Away from stops: standstills within 50 m of a stop are boarding, and within 150 m of a terminal are layovers; both are left out, and so are standstills longer than 5 minutes (breaks, breakdowns). Only lines in the city timetable count, since other operators' stops aren't known.
hotspots.how3: Hotspots: standstills are grouped where they gather (DBSCAN: standstills within 25 m of each other, at least 5 together) and a group needs at least 3 different buses. Time lost is the standing time altogether; slowing down and pulling away aren't included, so the real loss is larger.
hotspots.how4: Heading is the direction the buses faced while waiting, so a junction shows which approach holds them up. Busiest hour is the hour of the day with the most time lost.
hotspots.mapLabel: Map of stop hotspots by time lost

busLanes.eachIntro: A street's bus lanes in one direction. "Other way" is the same street in the opposite direction where it has no bus lane: the closest comparison, same traffic lights and stops. Click a row to show it on the map.
busLanes.fasterThanLane: Faster than on the bus lane
busLanes.none: No bus was recorded on a bus lane in this window.
busLanes.how1: Bus lanes are every street section OpenStreetMap tags with a lane for buses (busway, bus:lanes, psv:lanes, lanes:bus), fetched again every month. Length counts each direction's lane. Bus bays and terminus loops aren't lanes and are left out.
busLanes.how2: On a bus lane: each pair of consecutive position reports of a bus (5–90 s apart) counts where its middle is: on a lane when within 15 m of one and heading its way (within 45°). Within 30 m of a lane running the opposite way, it is on the same street the other way.
busLanes.how3: Speed is the distance driven over the time taken, stops and waits included, as passengers ride it. Layovers at termini, gaps over 90 s and GPS jumps are left out; only the timetable's lines inside the city count.
busLanes.how4: Delay change is how the delay the feed reports changed between the two reports, within one trip, per km driven: positive means buses fell further behind the timetable there, negative that they made up time (timetables allow for traffic, so buses often make up time on open roads).
busLanes.how5: Reading it: bus lanes are built on the most congested streets, through the centre with many stops and lights, so they are slower than the city's average however well they work. The fairer comparisons are the same street the other way without a lane, and how much slower each is at peak than off-peak: a lane that works keeps its peak speed.

delayGen.how1: Delay is the feed's (the operator's figure against the timetable), taken from the first report after a bus leaves each stop: the next stop it reports moves on by one. Reports come every 10 seconds, so one bus's figure is good to about ±10 seconds; averages over many buses are much closer.
delayGen.how2: A stretch's change is the delay on leaving the next stop minus the delay on leaving this one: the drive between them and the time standing at the next stop. Stretches where a report skipped a stop aren't measured, nor are delays over 30 minutes (feed errors). The last stretch of a run (arriving at the terminus) can't be measured.
delayGen.how3: Per day figures are over the days with recordings, and a stretch is shown once it was measured 5 times in the chosen part of the day. Only lines in the city timetable count.
delayGen.how4: Gained per run is the change from a run's first measured stop to its last (runs of 5 stops or more).

It is the smallest one holding every stop of the four timetables, with about 2 km to spare on each side for turning loops, depot runs and detours. Its furthest stops, all of Wschód Express: west Kołodzieje (line 470), east Kołpaki I (475), south Kaniuki II (474), north Uścianek (469). A timetable with stops further out needs it widened (ZBIORKOM_BIALYSTOK_BBOX).

corridors.intro: Stretches of at least 4 consecutive stops where two or more lines run together, joined end to end where the way on doesn't fork. Lines in an outlined badge run only part of a corridor. Both directions are one row. Peak: {{peak}}; off-peak: {{offPeak}}. Click a column to sort.
corridors.mapWidth: Buses in peak hours between stops · line width
corridors.mapColour: Buses in peak hours between stops · colour
corridors.oneWayCount: · {{n}} run one way only (the lines come back along other streets)

howText.corridor: Corridor: from the regular weekday timetable, in three steps.
howText.step1: For each set of 2 or more lines, the longest stretch of at least 4 consecutive stops they all run along.
howText.step2: A shorter one lying inside a longer one is dropped unless it carries at least 1.5 times as many buses (all of its stops), e.g. where an extra line joins for a few stops.
howText.step3: The rest are joined end to end where one ends on the stops the next starts with and the way on doesn't fork (all ways on lead to the same next stop). On a joined corridor, lines can join or leave partway: lines running all of it have a filled badge, lines running at least half of it an outlined one.
howText.busier: The stops, start and end shown are those of the busier direction.
howText.both: Both directions are one row when at least half of the lines run back between the same ends (stops with the same name, or less than 500 m apart) or along at least half of the same stops. Otherwise the row is marked "one way": in the centre, many lines go back along other streets.
howText.measured: Buses a day, interval and regularity are measured on each stretch between two stops (every bus using it) and averaged along the corridor, weighted by the stretches' length, so a line running part of it counts for that part. Buses: both directions added up; the rest averaged over the directions.
howText.interval: Interval: on each stretch, the minutes of the period divided by the buses leaving its first stop in it.
howText.regularity: Regularity: how evenly those buses are spread, as the coefficient of variation (CV) of the gaps between them: standard deviation ÷ mean, on each stretch per period window (needs 4 buses), weighted by the number of gaps. 0 means perfectly even. Lines sharing a corridor are rarely timed together, so corridors are usually less regular than single lines. Grades as in TCQSM: {{grades}}

col.regularityTitle: How evenly buses are spread: 0 = perfectly even

Like the woods, it is left out of the coverage and densities "without the woods and the Biała valley". The narrow stretch through the centre isn't counted.

coverage.beltIntro: Every village (sołectwo) and town reaching within {{km}} km of the city limits: {{places}} places, {{area}}, {{people}} residents in the {{known}} with a figure. On the map above with the districts, on the same scale; densities outside the woods, as for the districts.
coverage.how1: The city limits, districts, villages and woods come from OpenStreetMap ({{fetched}}). Areas are measured on a grid of {{cell}} m squares in the city and {{beltCell}} m squares around it, so overlapping woods count once.
coverage.how2: The Biała valley is the open land along the river (water, wetland, meadow, grassland, scrub, grass and parks in OpenStreetMap) where its valley is wide: from Piastowska along Branickiego to Stawy Dojlidzkie, and from Białostoczek west and north to the city limits; within 600 m of the river, outside the woods.
coverage.how3: Stops are those of the city's lines in the current timetable; one near the border also covers the city side of it. Distances are as the crow flies: walking along streets is longer.
coverage.how4: Residents of each district are those on the city's register at the end of 2025, for permanent or temporary stay ({{registered}} together). Statistics Poland puts the city at {{official}}: it counts everyone living here, registered or not, but has no figures by district. So the districts' densities are lower than the city's official one.
coverage.how5: Around the city, residents come from the gmina office for gmina Juchnowiec Kościelny (end of 2023) and from the 2021 census elsewhere; a few from Polish Wikipedia, with their year. Hover the date for the source. Places without a figure are left white.

routes.notInTimetable: Line {{line}} isn't in the city timetable: it is run by another operator. Below is only what was recorded on the live feed, on all days.
routes.recordedIntro: From every recorded position: {{runs}} runs (a bus's reports in a row towards one destination) between {{first}} and {{last}}, grouped by destination and the streets they took. Click a variant to show it on the map.
routes.noTimetable: No timetable yet. An admin can import it under Settings.
routes.speedBetween: Speed between stops in peak hours
routes.brigadesIntro: Each bus's duty on a weekday, from the timetable: it leaves the depot for its first run and returns after its last. Short gaps are layovers at the terminus; gaps of 30 minutes or more are marked as breaks.
routes.how1: Timetable figures use the regular weekday timetable. The base route of each direction is its most frequent variant; other variants are longer or shorter than it, or depot runs.
routes.how2: Scheduled average speed: distance divided by travel time of the base route's slowest and fastest scheduled run. Time at stops counts.
routes.how3: Regularity: how evenly departures are spread, as the coefficient of variation (CV) of the gaps between consecutive departures: standard deviation ÷ mean. It is measured at the first stop of the base route, counting every trip of the line that departs there, per direction and period (the break between the two peaks is not a gap), then averaged weighted by the number of gaps. 0 means perfectly even. Grades follow TCQSM: A ≤ 0.21, B ≤ 0.30, C ≤ 0.39, D ≤ 0.52, E ≤ 0.74, F above. For passengers arriving at random the average wait is half the mean gap × (1 + CV²), so uneven spacing adds waiting even at the same frequency. "—" means fewer than 4 departures in the period.
routes.how4: Standard end stops are where buses turn round in service: a brigade ends a run there and starts its next one within 30 minutes. Depot runs start or end away from them, as a brigade's first or last run or next to a break of 30 minutes or more. A variant is shown as a depot run when most of its trips are. A bus waiting longer at a standard end stop is on a break, not at the depot.
routes.how5: Nearby end stops: end stops less than 500 m apart, such as the arrival and departure platforms of a terminus, are shown as one, named after the stop where runs end. Every stop of such a group is within 500 m of all the others. This is a rule of thumb: a depot run's last stop can be close to a terminus (e.g. Branickiego/Świętojańska, 480 m from Piastowska/Pętla on line 103) and is still a depot stop, because no run turns round there. Depot-run stops are grouped the same way.
routes.how6: Zone 2: stops in fare zone 2 (outside Białystok). The zone border isn't in the timetable, so the stretch between the last city stop and the first zone-2 stop counts half.
routes.how7: Brigades come from the trip ids. The times at the row ends are the first departure and last arrival in the timetable; the drive between the depot and that stop isn't in it.
routes.how8: Full runs are runs of the base route or a longer variant recorded from the first stop to the terminus, on weekdays only, charted per route pattern (both directions together). Positions arrive about once a minute with the next stop, so the bus passed a stop between two reports: the midpoint is used (about ±30 s for a single run, rounded to minutes). Runs more than twice as long or half as short as the timetable are left out as faulty.
routes.how9: Average delay per 15 minutes, from every position report of the line on weekdays, except buses waiting at the first stop and reports over 30 minutes late (likely errors). Negative means early.
routes.how10: Vehicles come from every recorded day, weekends too. A bus seen for fewer than 5 reports on a brigade in a day is left out as a feed glitch, so it doesn't count as a vehicle change.
routes.how11: Speed between stops: total distance over total time of all peak-hour full runs on that stretch, so the timing error of single reports averages out. It includes time spent at the stop.
